title: Dalit Christians
hookLine: Indian Christians from communities once called untouchable

lines: WHO IS ALLOWED TO TOUCH WHOM?
A LEPER KNEELS IN THE ROAD.
cards: Who is allowed to touch whom? Societies keep quiet rules about it, and children pick them up early. In Mark's Gospel a man with a skin disease, a leper, kneels in the road in front of Jesus.
By the custom of the day, people kept their distance from him, and he kept his from them. He says, if you want to, you can make me clean.
And before Jesus says a word in reply, he does what everyone else had been careful not to do. He reaches out and touches him.

teach.h: AN ORDER THAT CALLED SOME UNTOUCHABLE.
teach.b: In India, caste has divided people for a long time, and at the bottom of that order were communities treated as untouchable: kept from wells, from temples, from the tables of others.
Dalit is a name people from these communities use for themselves today. Among India's Christians are Dalit families, and some of them heard their own story in that leper on the road.

teach.h: HE PUT FORTH HIS HAND, AND TOUCHED HIM.
teach.b: Mark tells it like this, in the King James Bible: "And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean." Touch first, then words.
Paul wrote something just as plain: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

teach.h: CASTE DID NOT STOP AT THE CHURCH DOOR.
teach.b: But caste did not stop at the church door. Dalit Christians and church leaders in India have spoken about separate seating, separate cemeteries, and pulpits closed to them in some places, inside the church itself.
So some Dalit Christian thinkers read the Bible from where they stood, and called it Dalit theology.
They noticed that Jesus himself was pushed out, and read Isaiah's line about the servant as their own: "He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief."
On that reading, God isn't at the top of the ladder looking down, but with the ones the ladder left out. Churches in India are still working out what that asks of them.

how: Dalit Christian communities in India worship in their own congregations and in mixed ones, and churches and Dalit theologians have taken up the fight against caste discrimination, including within the church.

games.q: a leper kneels in front of you in the road and says, if you want to, you can make me clean. the custom says keep your distance. what does Jesus do?
o: heals him with a word from a safe distance.
tells him to go to the priests first.
games.why: "Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him." the touch comes before the healing words.

practice: Think of someone you see often but never really greet: the person who cleans the office, the one who brings your packages, the relative everyone talks over at dinner, and notice whether you know their name.
Hold that face with the respect you'd give someone you admire. If you pray, pray for them by name, or by face if that's all you have; if not, simply wish them well.
